cross_file_conclusions.path: Setup local or LAN host -> ConfigureAndStart(chosen) -> MafiaReducer.submitDoctorProtect/resolveNight -> NightResolution -> private previous effective protection plus host nightLog -> MafiaSnapshotCodec/recoverMafiaSession -> local controller or bridge projections/rejoin.
proof: Existing doctorCanProtectSamePlayerConsecutively serialized flag remains default false; no duplicate setting or format change. Setup draft preserves it, while reducer rejects setup changes outside LobbySetup.

Authoritative reducer checks active/living Doctor actor and target, separate doctorCanSelfHeal, and nightChoiceSubmitted before changing pending choice. ON bypasses only consecutive-target restriction and has no two-night or other repetition cap.

Resolver derives effectiveDoctorTarget; reducer writes exactly that value to private previousDoctorProtect and resolved host night record. Explicit skip writes null and consumes the one submission. Dead Doctor is handled at resolution, not by inventing history.

Nonterminal recovery compares Doctor private previousDoctorProtect with newest retained nightLog.doctorProtect for both settings. OFF additionally validates adjacent retained history against repeat restriction; ON accepts legitimate repeated history.
First-night/no-Doctor null expectations, dead Doctor/target, day and night revotes, PostGame private cleanup, and retained 128-entry suffix are explicitly covered by common assertions.
Local and LAN target lists use DoctorTargetEligibility on living/active candidates. Settings propagate via authoritative public settings; peer command submission does not mutate canonical state.

Projection strips host logs, role map and seed before peer encoding; peers validate their own visible private state without receiving host history. Same-seat rejoin tests retain previous target, in-flight choice and settings.
cross_file_conclusions.compatibility: Existing serialized setting, snapshot 1.0.0, Mafia game wire2 and networking protocol domain are preserved. No migration introduced by current Doctor repair.
cross_file_conclusions.counter_evidence: Pure NightResolution is not the actor/action validation boundary; reducer owns legal self-target enforcement. PostGame intentionally clears private restrictions while preserving host history, so enforcing the active invariant there would reject legitimate terminal saves.
regression_source_evidence: 2 desktop MafiaDoctorLanTest methods, real bridge/coordinator over in-memory transport
cross_file_conclusions.limitations: In-memory bridge tests are not physical LAN; no Doctor app UI or native runtime executed by this reviewer.

cross_file_conclusions.path: WhodunitGameFlow local or WhodunitHostSessionFlow host replaces game subtree with SessionExitConfirmation -> DiscussionPhase LaunchedEffect disposed -> runDiscussionTickerLoop cancellation -> Stay remounts using retained canonical remaining seconds/timer ID.
proof: Leave-confirmation mounting stops presentation-owned ticks without submitting canonical Resume or subtracting wall-clock time. Stay merely clears modal state.
Canonical controller, writer and host networking are retained. Host lifecycle bridge may pause/resume canonical state but cannot create a UI ticker while the game subtree is absent.
Peer phase rendering is read-only for discussion; no peer owns the discussion timer or reducer.
Local and host regression tests cover repeated Leave/Stay, ticking resumes once, snapshot persistence, lifecycle changes, and manually paused state. No Mafia timed-round implementation was added.
cross_file_conclusions.limits: This records executable current behavior, not a newly invented timer product policy. Physical app-switch/lifecycle behavior remains root/device evidence.

proof: Readiness effect is bound to session, phase, own identity and assignment generation, and consults current atomic own projection immediately before command submission.
Already-recorded readiness does not auto-resubmit after presentation remount; host command/revision validation was not removed.
